title: The pain got better, then the belly went hard
objective: Recognize appendicitis with a positive Rovsing sign, and peritonitis after perforation as a route to sepsis
secondaryObjectives: Sepsis recognition and the first hour of response

brief.situation: 05:00 on a surgical unit. You are the RN for Mr. Becker, 24, admitted at 23:00 with suspected appendicitis: right lower quadrant pain, a positive Rovsing sign and a white count of 15,000. He is NPO with IV fluid running, waiting for the first case in the operating room at 08:00.
handover: At 03:00 he rated his pain 8/10 at McBurney's point.
At 04:30 he told the nursing assistant the pain 'suddenly got a lot better', and asked for a heating pad for his belly and a laxative because he 'hasn't gone in two days'.
Unit policy: the RN reports a change in abdominal findings or a positive sepsis screen to the surgical resident at once; blood cultures and lactate may be drawn on the sepsis standing order.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: Why did Mr. Becker's pain suddenly improve, and what do you do?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: In appendicitis, sudden relief of pain followed by a rigid, diffusely tender abdomen with fever and tachycardia means perforation and peritonitis, which leads to sepsis.
parts.modelAnswer: His appendix has probably ruptured. The pain eased when it burst, and now his belly is rigid and tender all over with a fever and a fast heart rate: peritonitis heading for sepsis.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Keeps him NPO with fluid running, avoids heat, laxatives and enemas, screens for sepsis with cultures and lactate, and calls the surgical resident at once.
parts.modelAnswer: Keep him NPO with the IV running, no heating pad and no laxative, do the sepsis screen with cultures and lactate, and call the surgical resident now.

shock.headline: Septic shock
shock.body: Sudden relief of appendicitis pain followed by a rigid, diffusely tender abdomen is perforation. Peritonitis leads to sepsis: screen, call the surgeon at once, and never apply heat or give a laxative.

safe.headline: Perforation caught
safe.body: You read the sudden relief as perforation, found peritonitis and sepsis, avoided heat and laxatives, and called within minutes. That is the expert path.

safeGaps.headline: Operated, with gaps

scoring.modelReasoning: Appendicitis brings pain at McBurney's point and a positive Rovsing sign (right lower quadrant pain when the left lower quadrant is pressed). Rising pressure can lead to rupture and peritonitis: the pain may ease suddenly, then the abdomen becomes rigid and diffusely tender with fever and tachycardia, and sepsis follows. Keep him NPO with IV fluid, avoid cathartics, enemas and heat on the abdomen, screen for sepsis with cultures and lactate, and call the surgeon at once.
